population.allocation: At least one per positive stratum, then largest remainder; individual estimate weight = target segment share / stratum sample count.

sources.title: Cathay Pacific Annual Report 2025 — HK Express operations
sources.supports: Low-cost leisure positioning, Asian destinations and aggregate passenger statistics; not the assumed target-segment weights.

sources.title: Cathay Group December 2025 traffic figures
sources.supports: Aggregate HK Express passenger counts and load factors; no matching membership conversion or segment-share table.

limitations: The reviewed official reports do not publish these customer distributions; all numerical segment weights and budget distributions remain test assumptions.
This is a deliberately targeted audience for flexible bargain travel, not a representative sample of all HK Express passengers. Fixed-date mandatory, urgent and business travel are excluded.
All sampled travellers are already valid members; no membership purchase, renewal, taxes, fuel fees or airline costs enter this experiment.
Each sampled member decides about one personal ticket; companions' purchases are outside this experiment.
Optional-trip interest, recent travel, destination appeal and the appeal of skipping are pre-price private scenario traits, not observed preferences or numerical willingness-to-pay labels.
Poststratified rates and expected revenue are estimates. Accepted ticket counts and cash revenue remain integer transactions in the cleared panel.
An LLM persona is not an independent observed HK Express customer; repeated choices do not create additional people.

decision.reason: The member fare of HKD 44 is a striking bargain, and Fukuoka is highly appealing today. analysis.summary: At the HKD 44 member fare, 16 of 32 customers bought, generating HKD 704 in basic receipts with no inventory denials and 42 quota units remaining. Most buyers cited the low fare as the decisive trigger, and several said they would decline or only reluctantly pay HKD 55. The 16 declines were all environment-forced budget/availability statements, not explicit price objections, so the evidence is mixed: strong conversion at the current fare but unclear headroom above it.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing a higher member fare on fresh customers will not reduce conversion enough to offset the higher per-ticket receipt, because many buyers described the fare as a bargain rather than a stretch.

analysis.summary: At HKD 30, 20 of 32 members bought the member fare, citing the low price as the decisive trigger; several said they would decline at HKD 55. Nine declines were environment-forced (no ticket both available and within budget), and three were low-interest optional-trip objections rather than price objections. No customer objected that HKD 30 was too expensive. The current fare sits well below the HKD 44 cap, so there is room to test a higher fare on fresh customers.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing a higher member fare on fresh members will keep conversion high enough that basic ticket receipts exceed those at HKD 30, since many buyers said the HKD 55 normal fare was still acceptable.

analysis.summary: At HKD 32, 18 of 32 customers bought the member fare, citing it as a compelling bargain that converted casual browsing into an optional trip. Most buyers said they would decline the HKD 55 regular fare, indicating the low price is decisive. Twelve declines were inventory-forced (no available ticket within budget), not price objections, and two were low-interest browsers. No customer objected to the fare itself. The cap is HKD 44, so a higher test is permitted.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing a higher member fare on fresh customers will show whether enough purchases remain to preserve or raise basic receipts, since many current buyers said they would decline at HKD 55.

analysis.summary: At the current HK$44 member fare (the permitted cap), 11 of 32 customers bought and 21 declined. Most declines (14) were environment-forced: no ticket both available and within budget, not a price objection. Four declines cited low interest or high outside option, and one cited low destination appeal with a recent trip. Buyers repeatedly called the fare compelling, and several said they would still pay the HK$55 normal fare. No customer objected to the fare itself as too high.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing a higher fare is not permitted since HK$44 is already the cap. A fresh paired test at the same HK$44 fare will reproduce conversion near the observed level; a materially lower conversion would contradict fare-neutrality of the current price.

Every decline cites no ticket both available and within basic-fare budget (environment-forced), not a stated price objection, and inventory denials are zero with seats and quota remaining. Buyers repeatedly call HKD 44 a bargain; several would pay the HKD 55 regular fare, while others would not. The current fare already sits at the permitted cap, so no higher test is allowed. Evidence supports retaining the fare on fresh customers rather than claiming optimality.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing the same HKD 44 member fare on fresh paired customers will reproduce a weighted conversion near 0.39; a materially lower conversion with unchanged inventory would contradict retaining this fare.

analysis.summary: At the 41 HKD member fare, 14 of 32 customers bought and 18 declined. Most declines (13) were environment-forced, reporting no ticket both available and within budget, which is an inventory/budget constraint rather than a stated price objection. Three declines cited low destination appeal or low trip interest with a strong outside option. Buyers repeatedly described 41 HKD as a compelling low fare, and several said they would still pay the 55 HKD normal fare. No customer explicitly objected to the fare level itself.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing a lower member fare on fresh customers will not meaningfully raise conversion, because most declines stem from availability/budget constraints and low trip interest rather than the 41 HKD fare level; conversion should stay near current levels.

analysis.summary: Of 32 members, 11 bought at the HKD 44 member fare and 21 declined. Most declines (17) were environment-forced: no ticket both available and within budget, which is an inventory/budget constraint rather than a stated price objection. Four declines cited low trip interest or a strong outside option despite finding 44 affordable. Buyers repeatedly called 44 a compelling bargain, and several said they would still pay 55. No customer explicitly rejected the fare as too expensive.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing a higher member fare on fresh customers will not reduce conversion enough to lower basic receipts, because buyers describe 44 as a bargain and several accept 55; a conversion drop exceeding the fare gain would contradict this.

initial_result.accounting: Base ticket receipts only; no membership fee, tax, fuel surcharge or operating costs.

analysis.summary: At the current 40 HKD member fare, 12 of 32 customers bought, generating 480 HKD in basic receipts. Most buyers cited the fare as a compelling bargain, and several said they would still pay the 55 HKD normal fare. Declines split between forced unavailability (11) and low-interest optional browsing (9), not price objections. No customer rejected the fare as too expensive. Evidence supports testing a higher fare on fresh customers, though buying at 40 HKD does not prove willingness to pay more.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing a higher member fare on fresh customers will not reduce weighted conversion enough to lower basic ticket receipts versus the current 40 HKD fare, since several buyers indicated willingness to pay the 55 HKD normal fare.

analysis.summary: At the current HKD 44 member fare, 13 of 32 customers bought and 19 declined. Twelve declines were environment-forced (no ticket both available and within budget), not price objections; four declines cited low interest or optional-trip priority, and three cited low interest with little destination pull. No customer objected to the fare itself as too high. Buyers repeatedly called 44 a bargain, and many said they would still pay the 55 normal fare. Evidence points to holding the fare rather than lowering it, though the cap limits upward testing.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing the same HKD 44 member fare on fresh customers will reproduce conversion near the observed 41%, with declines driven mainly by inventory/budget constraints and low trip interest rather than fare objections; a materially lower conversion would contradict this.

analysis.summary: At the HKD 44 member fare, 9 of 32 customers bought and 23 declined. Most declines (16) were environment-forced, with no ticket both available and within budget, not price objections. Six declines cited low trip interest or weak destination appeal despite finding HKD 44 affordable. Buyers described the fare as a compelling bargain, several would pay the HKD 55 normal fare. No customer objected to the fare itself as too high. Evidence points to holding rather than lowering, though the cap equals the current price.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing the same HKD 44 fare on fresh customers will yield a similar weighted conversion near 0.27; a materially lower conversion would contradict retaining this fare, while a materially higher one would suggest the current sample understates demand.

analysis.summary: At the current HKD 44 member fare (the permitted cap), 10 of 32 customers bought member tickets and 22 declined. Most declines cite no available ticket within their basic-fare budget (environment-forced), not a price objection. Among buyers, several would still pay the HKD 55 normal fare, while others would not. One decline reflects low trip interest rather than price. Since the fare is already at its cap, no higher test is permitted; evidence supports retaining the current fare for a fresh paired test.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing the same HKD 44 member fare on fresh customers will reproduce roughly one-third weighted conversion; if a fresh paired sample shows materially lower conversion at this fare, the retention assumption is contradicted.

analysis.summary: Of 32 members, 7 bought the 44 HKD member fare and 25 declined. Most declines (18) were environment-forced: no ticket both available and within budget, which is an inventory/budget constraint rather than a fare objection. Three declines cited low trip interest or optional leisure, not price. Buyers repeatedly said 44 HKD was a genuine bargain and several would not pay the 55 HKD regular fare. The current price sits at the permitted cap of 44, so no higher test is allowed.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing the same 44 HKD member fare on fresh members will reproduce roughly one-fifth weighted conversion, with most declines driven by budget/inventory constraints rather than fare level; a materially lower conversion would contradict this.

initial_result.accounting: Base ticket receipts only; no membership fee, tax, fuel surcharge or operating costs.

analysis.summary: At the current HKD 40 member fare, 13 of 32 customers bought, all citing the low fare as the decisive trigger; several explicitly said they would not pay the HKD 55 regular fare. Twelve declines were environment-forced (no available ticket within budget), and four were low-interest or recent-trip objections rather than price objections. No customer objected to the fare itself as too high. The fare sits below the HKD 44 cap, so a modest increase is testable, though buying at 40 does not prove willingness to pay more.
analysis.hypothesis: Raising the member fare modestly above HKD 40 for fresh customers will not reduce member conversion enough to lower total basic-ticket receipts, because most buyers cited the fare as a bargain well within budget.

initial_result.accounting: Base ticket receipts only; no membership fee, tax, fuel surcharge or operating costs.

analysis.summary: At the current 43 HKD member fare, 11 of 32 customers bought member tickets for 473 HKD in basic receipts, with no inventory denials and quota far from binding. Most declines (16) were environment-forced, meaning no offered ticket was both available and within budget, not a stated price objection. Three declines cited low interest or a recent trip rather than fare. Several buyers said they would not pay the 55 HKD normal fare, while a few would. No customer's primary reason is a price objection, so a lower-fare direction lacks the required cited decline.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing the same 43 HKD member fare on fresh paired customers will reproduce weighted conversion near 0.34 and basic receipts near 473 HKD; a materially lower conversion or receipts outcome would contradict retaining this fare.

analysis_attempts.error: A lower-price hypothesis needs a cited decline and a reported price objection

initial_result.accounting: Base ticket receipts only; no membership fee, tax, fuel surcharge or operating costs.

analysis.summary: At HKD 32, 19 of 32 customers bought the member fare, citing it as a compelling bargain below their budgets; several said they would decline at the HKD 55 regular fare. Nine declines were environment-forced (no ticket both available and within budget), and four were low-interest or recent-trip objections to an optional trip, not price objections. No customer objected to the fare itself as too high. The current price sits below the HKD 44 cap, leaving room to test a higher fare.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing a higher member fare on fresh customers will preserve enough purchases to raise basic ticket receipts, since buyers repeatedly described HKD 32 as well below their stated budgets and several would still pay the HKD 55 regular fare.

validation.scope: One purchase opportunity per member at the chosen flight snapshot, not annual membership profit.

assumptions: Only existing members; no joining or renewal decision and no fee deduction.
Base fares only; all taxes/fuel/add-ons and operating costs excluded. Revenue is not airline profit.
Population weights are explicit scenario assumptions, not measured HK Express market shares.
Fresh stratified members each search round; paired candidate and initial quote in reset, blinded worlds. One seat per member per world.
Only declared public segment/flexibility enter learning; private budgets, motivation and simulator constraints remain environment-only.
Every third round may test a cited LLM direction within a bounded model-scored interval; text never adds a demand label.
Analyst requests allow at most three attempts within the shared call budget. Unavailable analysis supplies no direction; recorded purchases still train Thompson and undergo independent confirmation.
Quoted fares are whole HKD; weighted averages and statistical estimates may have decimals.
Parallel intent elicitation followed by fixed-priority integer inventory clearing; no seat is reserved by an LLM.
Weighted demand estimates and actual panel cash/seat transactions are reported separately.
Final member quotes round down to an amount ending in nine, with any result below HK$30 becoming HK$0; raw search prices remain recorded.
Independent validation compares the formatted initial fallback, formatted selected fare and no offer after freezing both final quotes; no refitting on holdout.
